title: Backflow preventer troubleshooting: identify the symptom before choosing a fix
description: Troubleshooting begins by locating water or failure evidence at the relief opening, test cock, cover, shutoff, union, body, or connected pipe.
prompt: What is the observable symptom and exactly where is it occurring?
answer: Troubleshooting begins by locating water or failure evidence at the relief opening, test cock, cover, shutoff, union, body, or connected pipe. The symptom routes the next inspection; it does not name the failed part by itself.
urgency: Escalate uncontrolled discharge, flooding, electrical or fire-system exposure, body damage, or an assembly that cannot be identified.
identifiers: A relief opening, cover seam, test cock, and piping joint are different leak locations.
The current model and size determine whether a service path can be verified.
A failed certified test report contains useful component-level evidence.

choices.label: I know the model and size
choices.detail: Use model-specific sources before ordering parts or accepting a repair scope.

choices.label: The assembly is leaking or failed
choices.detail: Document the location and obtain a qualified diagnosis before repair.

choices.label: The body may be damaged
choices.detail: Compare repair with a complete replacement and retest scope.

steps.title: Observe and identify
steps.body: Identify the leak or failure location without touching internal components.

steps.title: Match the verified path
steps.body: Match the observed location to model-specific service literature and a qualified diagnosis.

steps.title: Close the risk loop
steps.body: Confirm repair, retest, and reporting responsibilities before work begins.

safeChecks: Photograph the full assembly and close-up symptom area.

stopConditions: Water discharge is uncontrolled or threatens property.
The symptom is paired with a cracked or distorted body.
